A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same crosscoder study. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and complete appendices are readable and support matching content across revisions and relocations.

before.justification: V2 reports original crosscoder training, Latent Scaling analyses, causal interventions, autointerpretability, and latent steering experiments, including Gemma and Llama results.

after.justification: V3 retains these empirical results and adds original analyses of medical specialization and further RL reasoning training in Appendix I.2.

M1.justification: The crosscoder architectures, sparsity mechanisms, inference thresholding, and operational Latent Scaling targets remain unchanged in Appendices B and E.2. V3 introduces scaling through raw activations as explanatory groundwork; it does not establish a changed training or inference procedure.

E1.justification: Appendix I.2 extends coverage beyond base-to-chat tuning to medical specialization using Gemma/Meditron3 and further RL reasoning training using DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen/Nemotron. New crosscoder data include BioInstruct, medical-o1-reasoning-SFT, MedRAG/PubMed, and OpenR1-Math-220k. Existing web/chat and Llama coverage remains.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the L1/BatchTopK comparison, Latent Scaling versus norm-based rankings, and existing intervention controls. Both alternative BatchTopK variants were already evaluated in v2 Appendix B.3. The added domain experiments reuse the same comparator set.

E3.justification: The new domain experiments specify 89M-token medical and 100M-token reasoning crosscoder training mixtures, comparable validation L0 near 100, and false-attribution summaries using a 0.6 scaling-ratio cutoff. V3 also drops normalization from the reported norm-difference formula while retaining classification cutoffs, creating a metric inconsistency; the retained results do not establish rerunning existing experiments.

E4.justification: Appendix I.2 adds substantive robustness tests of whether Complete Shrinkage and Latent Decoupling extend beyond base-to-chat tuning. Figures 16–17 examine medical and RL reasoning model pairs through norm histograms, error/reconstruction scatterplots, and specificity-threshold curves. Earlier variant ablations, cosine-twin analyses, and steering cases remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same 95% confidence-interval practice for causal-intervention results and retain correlation significance reporting. V3 adds no repeated-run, seed, uncertainty-estimation, or significance-testing procedure.

E6.justification: New Table 1 reports false-attribution and threshold counts across five model pairs. It classifies 235/246 medical L1 FT-only latents (95.5%) and 58/59 reasoning L1 latents (98.3%) as false; BatchTopK selects zero FT-only latents in both new domains. Retained headline results are unchanged. Section 3.3 removes the finding that 67% of chat-only latents have at least one-third of activations on template tokens.

T1.justification: V3 corrects the printed reconstruction-ratio denominator and adds Appendix E.1's binary-activation derivation connecting beta to magnitude times conditional probability. However, v2's normalized norm-difference definition becomes an unnormalized formula in v3 Equation 3, and the new glossary incorrectly defines reconstruction errors as differences between base and chat activations. Core loss and scaling derivations remain.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and concluding discussion retain the central contributions: diagnosing two L1 sparsity artifacts, introducing Latent Scaling, mitigating artifacts with BatchTopK, and identifying interpretable, causally relevant chat-specific latents. Added experiments support these existing claims.

C2.justification: Section 5 newly qualifies generalization across layers and acknowledges uncertainty about dictionary width and sparsity. Appendix I.2 interprets the added domain experiments as evidence of broader generality. Existing limitations concerning residual behavioral information and distinguishing novel concepts from shifted activation patterns remain.

D1.justification: Appendix I.2 supplies checkpoint identifiers and corpus mixtures/token counts for the added experiments. Existing implementation and compute details remain. Although the reproducibility appendix is replaced, its code, training-library, model, notebook, and training-log links remain in the first-page footnote.

R1.justification: V3 adds citations to Shah et al. on ModelDiff, Skean et al. on layer representations, and sources for the medical/reasoning models and datasets. The main related-work discussion and positioning relative to crosscoders and sparse autoencoders remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The central method exposition is substantially rewritten around encoder/decoder intuition and a raw-activation-first explanation of scaling. Section 3.2 reorganizes baselines and rewrites result interpretation. A substantial terminology/notation glossary replaces Appendix A, and Appendix I is reorganized into Llama and specialized-domain subsections.

P2.justification: V3 adds Table 1 and two four-panel figures for the domain experiments, revises explanatory captions, and adopts NeurIPS typography and spacing. Existing figures and tables largely retain their designs, with resizing, reflow, relocation, and renumbering.

improvement.justification: The added domain experiments strengthen evidence beyond chat-tuning, while expanded explanations and explicit layer/hyperparameter limitations help readers. However, v3 replaces v2's correctly normalized norm metric with an inconsistent formula and introduces incorrect glossary residual definitions. Its new zero false-attribution percentages also concern empty BatchTopK FT-only selections. These problems affect interpretation and reproducibility of the expanded evidence, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
